title: Latest stable Next.js bundles a vulnerable PostCSS version
description: npm audit reports GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 through Next.js 16.2.10's private PostCSS 8.4.31 dependency. The root PostCSS is patched, but npm's automated fix proposes downgrading Next.js to 9.3.3.
error_message: 2 moderate severity vulnerabilities; fixAvailable: next@9.3.3 (SemVer major).
root_cause: The current stable Next.js package pins a private PostCSS release below 8.5.10, and npm overrides do not replace that nested bundle safely.
solution: Removed the ineffective override, documented the upstream risk, retained patched root PostCSS 8.5.19, and rejected npm audit fix --force because it would downgrade the framework across major versions. The app does not stringify user-controlled CSS.

strategies: Re-run npm audit when Next.js releases an updated stable package
Never apply audit force-fixes that silently downgrade the application framework
Do not feed untrusted user content into CSS stringification
code_patterns: Avoid: npm audit fix --force without reviewing the proposed dependency graph
Use: explicit risk documentation until the upstream stable package is patched
tests_to_add: Run npm audit during dependency upgrade verification

title: Protected-route proxy was outside the src application root
description: The auth proxy was created at repository root even though this Next.js app uses src/app, so Next did not include it in the production middleware manifest.
error_message: Unauthenticated GET /rooms/demo returned a streamed 200 redirect and middleware-manifest.json was empty.
root_cause: Proxy placement followed the repository root convention without accounting for the project's src-based App Router layout.
solution: Moved proxy.ts to src/proxy.ts and retained the Server Component identity check as defense in depth.

strategies: Place proxy.ts beside app when the application uses a src directory
Inspect the production middleware manifest and assert an HTTP redirect during auth smoke tests
tests_to_add: Assert middleware-manifest.json contains the proxy after build
Assert unauthenticated /rooms/demo responds with a Location header to /login

title: Authenticated context read the cookie-backed session user
description: After validating claims, the server context also accessed session.user.id, which Supabase correctly warns is sourced from untrusted cookie storage.
error_message: Using the user object as returned from supabase.auth.getSession() could be insecure.
root_cause: A redundant consistency comparison accessed the session user even though getClaims had already established the trusted identity.
solution: Use only getClaims().claims for identity and use getSession solely to retrieve the access token after validation.

strategies: Never authorize with a user object returned from getSession
Use validated claims for userId/email and limit session access to the token
tests_to_add: Fail authenticated HTTP smoke tests on Supabase insecure-session-user warnings

title: Broad environment search printed a browser-visible legacy key
description: A repository-wide search for Supabase public-key variable names also matched the local .env file and printed the configured legacy anon key in diagnostic tool output. The key is intentionally browser-visible and was already documented as stale, but environment values should not be emitted during source inspection.

context.code_snippet: rg matched .env while searching for NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE key names

error_message: A public Supabase anon-key value appeared in command output.
root_cause: The search excluded dependencies and build output but did not exclude .env files or restrict output to filenames and variable names.
solution: Stopped using the legacy browser key for the feature, kept password recovery server-side, and adopted environment-safe searches that exclude .env values or print only matched filenames.

strategies: Exclude .env and credential files from repository-wide content searches
Inspect .env.example for configuration contracts instead of local .env values
Use rg --files-with-matches or redact values when environment inspection is unavoidable
code_patterns: Avoid: rg KEY_PATTERN . without an .env exclusion
tests_to_add: Keep secret-scanning checks in the release gate
